what_this_is: The questions the method has put to its world whose answers are published, each with the status its own record gives it. A result that went against us stays.

loop.why: the improvement loop has not gone round yet: its register is built once the current correctness work is finished (the director's ruling of 26 Oct)

rows.question: Does pricing each renewal for the customer earn more than one margin for everyone?
rows.why_this_status: the comparison marks itself provisional: its figures were measured in 2 different worlds, so the spread from one cannot bound the figure from another

rows.question: Did the flat-margin arm price exactly the same renewals as the per-customer arm?
rows.finding: It prices the same renewals through the same guards under the same lawful ceiling.
rows.why_this_status: it was a claim about a RUN, written as a module constant, and no run this page has ever published made it true.

rows.question: For accounts opened under the price cap, does sizing the first direct debit from an estimate beat waiting for the first bill?
rows.finding: Once a fabric premise's registry EAC is its own reads in the record the DD opening reads, the estimate beats the first bill on the households opened under the price cap: the matched mean change in distance from square goes negative, with a 95% interval that excludes zero.
rows.why_this_status: a prediction filed on 2026-10-01, before the run, which the run did not refute: across 95 matched accounts the estimate moved the direct debit £154.50 closer to the bill on average (95% interval £61.50 to £236.08 closer), on the billed clock

rows.question: For accounts opened under the price cap, does sizing the first direct debit from an estimate beat waiting for the first bill? (as published on 2026-09-03)
rows.finding: Sizing the opening direct debit from an estimate cut year-one drift by about £200 per household, with a 95% interval that excluded zero.
rows.why_this_status: A re-run on 1 Oct put the same price-cap population at £33.68 closer, with a 95% interval from £157.94 closer to £163.55 further, so we could no longer tell the two rules apart. Holding households and bills fixed, the rule change was worth £3.27; the collapse came with the run, where four households whose registry consumption figure was a fraction of their own use set the mean.

rows.question: Do the reviewers that pass finished work catch the defects that later surface?
rows.why_this_status: 0 of the 1 reviewer whose passes are traced to later defects has the 3 passes a measured error rate needs; the blind reviews in the review ledger are not traced to later defects at all
